subject: Backplane latency allocation inquiry - customer-managed ONTAP
messages:
From: Lillian Chan <lillian.chan@edgecore.io>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 5 Dec 2026 08:14:00 -0800
Subject: Backplane latency allocation for private deployment — request for exception

Hi Kimberly,

We're stood up with the private deployment for our ONTAP-backed cluster (customer-managed backplane) and are seeing tail latency events that look like they're originating inside our backplane fabric during scale-out operations. We understand Redwood's private SLA assumes control-plane network fabric under the customer's purview in these setups, but the procurement team flagged the need to get an explicit carveout in writing for latency attribution so the execs can sign off.

Quick details:
- Environment: EdgeCore private VPC (ONTAP backplane, customer-controlled NIC bonding)
- Observed symptom: 99.99th percentile token latency spikes up to 1.2s for ~30–90s during background compaction/reshuffle
- Impact: affects throughput for batch inference; not affecting token generation correctness

Can Redwood provide (a) a short exception template we can present to legal that delineates attribution for backplane-origin latency, and (b) a list of evidence/telemetry items we should collect so this can be triaged without triggering an SLA incident? Attaching our current network diagram and a short pcap sample.

Thanks — appreciate quick guidance, we are on a tight procurement timeline.

Best,
Lillian
Platform Ops, EdgeCore Inc.
attachments: edgecore-network-diagram.pdf, pcap-sample-20261204.pcap

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Lillian Chan <lillian.chan@edgecore.io>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 5 Dec 2026 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Backplane latency allocation for private deployment — request for exception

Hi Lillian — thanks for the detail and the diagrams. Short answers first: yes, we can do a narrowly-scoped SLA attribution exception for customer-controlled backplane events provided there is mutually-agreed evidence and a remediation/runbook in place. 

What we'll need from you to move fast:
- Telemetry package: prefix/KV cache hit rates, per-request token latency distribution (p50/p95/p99/p99.99) for the affected windows, server-side kernel timestamps (submit->dispatch->completion), and the pcap you attached.
- Runbook: a short on-call playbook that describes compaction/reshuffle windows and mitigation steps (we looked at a draft and attached a small runbook template below).
- Delegated monitoring: a cross-account read-only telemetry role or shared dashboards so our SREs can validate the evidence without creating an SLA incident immediately.

Proposed exception language (draft, please run by legal):
"Redwood's availability and latency SLAs for Private deployments exclude latency events demonstrably caused by customer-managed backplane operations (including but not limited to compaction, reshuffle, or firmware-induced NIC flap events). Such exclusion applies only when (1) the customer provides telemetry evidencing network/backplane origin agreed by both parties, (2) a documented mitigation runbook is in place, and (3) the customer implements a monitoring share for Redwood SREs to validate incidents. In the absence of sufficient telemetry, Redwood may treat incidents as SLA-affecting until proven otherwise."

If that language looks acceptable we can turn it into a short addendum and do a single-signature DocuSign. In parallel, Naomi / Aditya — could you review the proposed evidence list and confirm retention window expectations (I propose 30 days for kernel timestamps and 90 days for aggregated latency histograms).

Lillian — if you can push the telemetry and a runbook link to the Drive link in my email we can review and fast-track. I also created a ticket (SUP-6127) to track the legal signoff.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Head of Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
attachments: edgecore-runbook-v1.pdf

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 5 Dec 2026 11:18:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Backplane latency allocation for private deployment — request for exception

Naomi / Aditya — forwarding EdgeCore's request and my draft exception language below. High level ask from procurement: a carveout that keeps our SLA economics intact when the backplane (customer-owned) is at fault. My proposed constraints:
- Evidence must show network/backplane origin (pcap + kernel timestamps + cached KV miss patterns)
- Customer must provide a runbook and a rehearsal scheduled within 14 days of exception approval
- Retention: kernel timestamps 30 days, histograms 90 days (proposed)

Can you: (1) sanity-check the wording for operational feasibility, (2) confirm retention windows and whether SUP should auto-close if no telemetry is provided within 7 days, and (3) flag any legal concerns we should be aware of before I share this as a DocuSign addendum?

Quoted text follows.

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Lillian Chan <lillian.chan@edgecore.io>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Dec 2026 16:44:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Backplane latency allocation for private deployment — exception addendum signed

Hi Lillian — following our reviews with product and SRE, and after the runbook walk-through yesterday, Redwood is able to accept a narrowly-scoped SLA attribution exception for the EdgeCore private deployment. Summary of the agreed items:

- Scope: exclusion applies to transient latency spikes where evidence demonstrates the root cause is customer-managed backplane operations (compaction/reshuffle/firmware-led NIC flap).
- Evidence required: pcap + per-request kernel timestamps (submit/dispatch/complete) + aggregated latency histograms for the affected window.
- Retention: kernel timestamps 30 days, latency histograms 90 days.
- Operational precondition: customer must publish a mitigation runbook and schedule a 30-minute runbook rehearsal with Redwood within 14 days of exception signing.
- Exception duration: 12 months subject to renewal; Redwood reserves the right to re-open attribution if evidence is insufficient during an incident.

Attached is the signed addendum (DocuSign) and our runbook template. We will keep SUP-6127 open for tracking. Please confirm the rehearsal date and upload the telemetry package to the Drive link so SREs can validate the first incident if/when it occurs.

Best regards,
Kimberly Park
Head of Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
attachments: signed-exception-docusign.pdf, edgecore-runbook-v1.pdf
